title: cost-optimization: autotune batching & caching defaults, add quantization profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Malik
description: Motivation: reduce per-token serving cost and operational overhead by making sensible defaults for batching and caching available out-of-the-box, provide vetted quantization profiles to safely lower GPU memory and throughput costs, and surface unit-economics tooling in the Console to allow engineers to simulate cost impact before rolling changes. Changes in this PR implement an autotune path that computes recommended batching and prefix/KV caching defaults based on observed request distributions, latency SLOs, and model characteristics. We add a small stateful autotuner that runs on the serving control plane and writes defaults to config with a conservative decay policy. We introduce a first set of quantization profiles (int8/4-bit candidates) in runtime/quant/profiles.yaml along with a validation shim that runs quick quality checks against a small eval prompt set; quant profiles are gated behind a feature flag and require explicit opt-in for Dedicated/Private installs. We add a Console export and simulation tool (console/unit_econ/tooling.py + UI hooks) that consumes traffic stats, model profile, and autoscale parameters to estimate per-call and per-100k-token unit economics. Migration notes: default behavior is backward-compatible; autotune is off by default for existing clusters and enabled for new clusters created after the release. Rollout: staged canary (10% of serving traffic with canary model routing) -> 50% -> full; automatic rollback if quality regression >1.5% on the eval set or latency p95 increase >10%. Testing: unit and integration tests cover autotuner heuristics, caching TTL changes, and quantization validation. Benchmarks show median per-token cost improvements of 8-15% on typical assistant workloads with no measurable quality regressions for the recommended profiles. See release notes and docs for guidance and opt-in flags.

release_notes: Adds autotuning for batching and caching defaults to reduce per-token cost
Introduces model quantization profiles and a validation shim for safe opt-in
Adds unit economics export and Console tooling to simulate cost impact before rollout
Staged canary rollout with automatic rollback on quality or latency regressions
notes_for_ops: Autotune disabled by default for existing clusters. To enable: set cluster.feature_flags.autotune=true and configure a conservative decay and eval set. Quantization requires explicit opt-in and a validation eval set. See docs/ops/autotune-migration.md for scripts and rollback procedures.
